content: The test image shows a soybean stem with dark brown/reddish-brown discoloration running longitudinally along the stem, with green pods nearby. This looks like a stem canker or stem blight disease. Top candidates: Diaporthe, Phomopsis, Anthracnose.

Analyzing the evidence:

**Test image observations:**
- Stem close-up showing dark brown/reddish-purple longitudinal discoloration running along the stem
- Green pods still present (mid-season timing)
- Discoloration spans most of the visible stem length
- Hairy/pubescent stem texture with continuous brown necrotic streak

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Diaporthe**: Shows dark brown longitudinal stem canker lesions — matches the test image well (elongated brown stem necrosis, mid-season with green pods)
- **Phomopsis**: Primarily shows pod symptoms — circular dark spots/pycnidia on pods — doesn't match the stem-focused lesion
- **Anthracnose**: Shows late-season dry/golden tissue with dark pod spots — doesn't match the fresh green-pod + brown stem pattern

The dark reddish-brown longitudinal stem canker with green pods is the hallmark of Diaporthe stem canker (Diaporthe phaseolorum var. caulivora).
